cards.text: This song is by David, Israel's king, who kept his father's sheep when he was young (1 Samuel 16:11). He opens with one line that sets up the whole song: "The LORD is my shepherd". Friend, a sheep with THAT shepherd? That sheep is SET.

cards.question: Because the LORD is his shepherd, David says he will never ___ anything he needs.

cards.text: The LORD makes David lie down in green pastures and leads him beside quiet waters. My best nap in that junk drawer was on a pile of old takeout menus, and friend, that was NOT green pastures.

cards.question: Green pastures and quiet waters. What's the feel of this picture David paints?

cards.text: A tired sheep gets to lie down, eat and drink, and it comes back to life. David says the LORD does that kind of thing on the inside too.

cards.question: On the inside, David says the LORD does this for his soul: He ___ it.
Next, the LORD guides David in the paths of righteousness. David says the LORD does it because David earned it.

cards.text: Then the road turns, and David walks through the valley of the shadow of death. That's the stretch of road where you turn the radio DOWN so you can see better.

cards.question: Even in the valley of the shadow of death, David says he will fear no evil. Why?

answers.text: Because the LORD is with him

cards.question: Up to the valley, David talks about the LORD: He makes me lie down, He leads me. In the valley, David starts talking right to the LORD instead.

cards.text: Out in that dark valley, David thinks about the shepherd's rod and staff. Now, a big stick in a scary place could go either way, right?

cards.question: In the valley of the shadow of death, what does David say the LORD's rod and staff do for him?

cards.text: Then the picture flips. No more sheep in a field: David's a guest now, and the LORD is the host.

cards.question: Like a host welcoming a guest, the LORD prepares a ___ for David.
David says the LORD prepares his table far away from his enemies.

cards.text: Then the LORD anoints David's head with oil. Friend, the last thing anybody poured on MY head was drawer dust.

cards.question: At the LORD's table, David says his cup overflows. What is that picture saying?

cards.text: Last line, and David looks ahead at the rest of his life. No five-year plan here, friend. This one covers ALL the days.

cards.question: With a shepherd and host like the LORD, what does David say will follow him all the days of his life?
To close his song, where does David say he will dwell forever?

answers.text: In the house of the LORD

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'This song is by David...', 'He opens with one line...', 'Friend, a sheep with THAT shepherd?' and 'That sheep is SET.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card says 'David says the LORD does that kind of thing on the inside too.' That claims David links the sheep resting and drinking in verse 2 to the LORD restoring his soul in verse 3. The text never makes that link. It only says 'He restores my soul.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card turns the BSB's 'Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death' into a plain statement: 'David walks through the valley of the shadow of death.' It drops the 'though.'

The joke 'That's the stretch of road where you turn the radio DOWN so you can see better' points 'That' at the Bible valley itself. This blends the modern car-and-radio picture into David's valley instead of keeping the comparison as its own image.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The true or false asks whether David switches from talking about the LORD ('He') to talking to Him ('You') in the valley. No earlier card shows the 'You' wording. Cards 8 and 9 only paraphrase verse 4 ('the LORD is with him'). So the baker can't reason out the pronoun shift and can only guess.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: This story card isn't the opening card, but it has 3 sentences: 'Last line, and David looks ahead...', 'No five-year plan here, friend.' and 'This one covers ALL the days.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
